reframing_when: The question asks about a low-leverage intervention when a higher-leverage point of intervention exists in the same system — the question is about the 80% of effort that produces 20% of results.
The question treats all interventions as equally promising without prioritizing based on which variables the team can actually influence and which have the biggest system-wide impact.
The question asks 'how do we improve X?' when X is a downstream metric driven by an upstream variable Y that the question doesn't mention — the question is chasing the effect, not the cause.
The question is about optimizing within the current paradigm when the highest leverage point is changing the paradigm itself — the system resists this change, which is why the question avoids it.
reframing_move: Shift the question upstream: instead of asking about the metric or symptom, ask 'what is the highest-leverage variable in this system, and are we asking the right question about it?' — the Pareto reframe directs the question toward the 20% of variables that drive 80% of outcomes.
curation_note: Leverage points operates on question framing by redirecting inquiry from low-leverage to high-leverage intervention points. The source is explicit: the model demands 'focusing on issues that have the biggest impact and that they can actually influence.' The paradigm-level leverage point (the highest tier) is the most powerful reframing move — changing what the system believes, not what it does.

reframing_when.note: All four activations grounded: low vs high leverage (Pareto principle), influence-based prioritization (problem disaggregation), upstream vs downstream (return on capital tree), and paradigm change (highest-order leverage point).

frame_patterns_challenged.note: Proxy optimization: the question optimizes a downstream metric when the upstream driver is the real lever. Scope lock: the question's scope excludes the highest-leverage intervention because it would require changing the paradigm.
